text:
Ravi: Bringing up 'zephyr-hybrid-13b' (Llama head layout + Mistral-style rotary). Int4 quantized build shows tight logits early but output entropy collapses after ~12 tokens, lots of repetition. Suspect rotary freq or KV index mismatch.
Anya: Can you drop a tiny repro + quant settings? Also confirm tokenizer converter used and whether BOS/EOS ids were remapped.
Ravi: repro: 
```
prompt = \"TL;DR: The CEO announced...\"
ids = conv_tok.encode(prompt)
out = model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=80, use_kv_cache=True)
print(out)
```
Quant: int4-aq + per-channel bias correction, act-order=\"proj_act\", no calibration table (fast path). Converter: llama2->zephyr-conv v3 with --preserve-ids.
Luke: act-order=proj_act can flip weight layout expectations. Which runtime path are you using? our AVX int4 kernel expects proj then act, while the converter sometimes emits act-first layouts for head-interleaved configs.
Ravi: runtime is the new int4_avx path (default). Convert log contains: \"warning: head_interleave=true assumed; emitting interleaved proj layout\" but runtime printed nothing about interleave on load.
Sana: quick test: run fp16 (no quant) with identical converter artifacts and compare logits per token when kvcache=True. If divergence appears as soon as cached keys are read, it's a KV ordering bug.
Ravi: did fp16 vs int4 compare. Diff table (max abs per token): 0, 3e-7, 1e-6, 2e-5, 0.08, 0.11, 0.12, 0.49, 0.52, ... so big jump at tokens 7-8.
Anya: token 7-8 jump strongly suggests either head ordering or rotary phase mismatch (wrap). Do you have rotary_base/freq_scale in converter metadata?
Ravi: converter metadata: \"rotary_base\": 10000, \"freq_scale\": 1.0, \"rotary_variant\": \"mistral-adapter\". Runtime reported rotary_base=10000 but freq_scale defaulted to 0.5 for this layout (I think).
Luke: that's the mismatch. If converter emitted freq_scale=1 but runtime used 0.5, phase accumulation will differ once kv cache is used (older tokens get scaled differently). Try forcing runtime freq_scale=1.0 via env var and re-run.
Sana: also verify head_interleave flag in the loaded model object: model.config.get('head_interleave') vs converter manifest. We added a small assert in converters/convert_utils.py that compares proj reshape order; it would have flagged this.
Ravi: ran two quick probes: (1) set runtime freq_scale=1.0 -> repetition reduced, perplexity closer to fp16 baseline; (2) toggled head_interleave to true in runtime loader -> logits aligned almost exactly with fp16 by token 5.
Anya: good signal: both fixes help, head_interleave mismatch is likely primary. We should patch converter to emit explicit 'head_interleave' tag in manifest and add runtime loader assert.
Luke: add a short smoke test to onboarding CI: load converted model int4, generate 32 tokens on canonical prompt with kvcache=True and assert token-level top1 matches fp16 for first N tokens or within tiny epsilon. If mismatch -> fail.
triage-bot: New label applied: onboarding/zephyr-hybrid. Assigned to @Anya and @Luke. Add onboarding board card: /board onboarding/handoffs. :pushpin:
Sana: I'll open a quick PR to (1) write head_interleave into converter manifest, (2) add runtime loader warning if manifest and runtime default disagree, and (3) CI smoke test comparing int4->fp16 logits for canonical prompt.
Ravi: thanks all, running extended eval now (phase sweep +/- 0.25, 0.5 multipliers) and will paste numeric table. Initial results: freq_scale=1.0 + head_interleave=true gave near-fp16 outputs; freq_scale 0.5 gave the degenerate repeats. Will follow up with artifacts in onboarding board.
